causal_graphs.context: Cells are de-energized with 0.5 mM 2,4-dinitrophenol for 40 min at 30 C, washed three times, diluted to OD660 0.5 and loaded with 2 uM ethidium in 50 mM KPi, 5 mM MgSO4, pH 7.0 at 30 C. Glucose initiates efflux; Methods specify 12.5 mM glucose but Figure 2 specifies 20 mM. The comparison is 1 mM added Na+ versus no added Na+, with the 400-s fluorescence endpoint and three independently prepared cell batches, mean +/- SEM.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 2A, its caption, and transport Methods establish the sodium-versus-no-added-sodium endpoint. The retained context records the conflicting glucose concentrations explicitly.
Current UniProt/InterPro sequence equality and the historical AAF94694.1 comparison establish the mapped intact protein, without transferring the assay to isolated repeats.
evidence.snippet: Q9KRU4 Pfam:PF01554; repeat intervals: 17-176 and 243-404, inclusive.

edges.mechanism: Added sodium lowers the normalized fluorescence endpoint relative to no added sodium in the NorM-VC-expressing host, consistent with enhanced ethidium efflux. The matched control host and the separate NorM-PS comparison constrain attribution; neither a physical ion path nor antibiotic resistance in Vibrio is measured here.
edges.subject: sodium-added-norm-cells

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q9KRU4 / norM / VC_1540, V. cholerae O1 N16961, has current PF01554 repeats at 17-176 and 243-404 in the 457-aa sequence version 2. The paper's AAF94694.1 reference is 461 aa; its residues 6-461 exactly match current 2-457, with different N-terminal initiation. This reference reconciliation does not independently resequence the N-terminal His10 assay plasmid. Intact protein is tested, not isolated repeats.
causal_graphs.limitations: Intracellular ethidium-associated fluorescence is an efflux proxy, not an absolute mass-flux measurement. Sodium addition also changes cellular energetics; the edge does not establish an isolated sodium-binding step or ion stoichiometry. Nonexpressing controls lack the comparable sodium response. The glucose discrepancy remains unresolved. No universal sodium requirement is inferred from this pH-7 comparison.

nodes.label: Add 1 mM Na+ to glucose-energized NorM-VC-expressing cells

causal_graphs.scope: His10-tagged V. cholerae NorM-VC expressed in L. lactis NZ9000 delta lmrA delta lmrCD, Raturi 2021 Figure 2A; not a native Vibrio phenotype or all MatE proteins.
causal_graphs.title: Added sodium lowers the ethidium fluorescence endpoint in NorM-VC-expressing cells

causal_graphs.context: Protein is purified from L. lactis membranes using DDM and Ni-NTA. Titrations contain 2 uM ethidium, 50 mM KPi pH 7.0, 0.2 mM KCl and 0.05% DDM, with 0.036-1 uM protein and either no added sodium or 0.5 mM Na2SO4 (1 mM Na+). Fluorescence anisotropy uses 500/580 nm excitation/emission after about 2 min equilibration and matched elution-buffer baseline. Three independent protein preparations are reported, mean +/- SEM.

evidence.explanation: Figure 4A's WT sodium and no-addition curves, biochemical Results and binding Methods support the scoped increase. The high-concentration convergence is preserved.

edges.mechanism: With sodium, WT anisotropy rises more strongly at low protein concentrations than without sodium. The response supports sodium-modulated ethidium binding in detergent, not sodium-driven transmembrane transport by this preparation.
edges.subject: sodium-added-purified-wt

evidence.explanation: Figure 4A's D36N paired curves were compared with WT and the Results; current D32 mapping is retained separately from paper numbering.

edges.mechanism: D36N lacks the WT positive sodium-dependent high-affinity component while retaining ethidium-associated anisotropy. This is loss of the sodium response, not complete loss of binding or direct observation of protonation.
edges.subject: d36n-versus-wt

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 4A and the matching mutation Results support the response loss, not a general loss of ligand binding.

edges.mechanism: E255Q removes the WT positive sodium enhancement, with nearly overlapping sodium/no-sodium titrations. Its residual anisotropy is not described as a binding-null phenotype, and the assay does not isolate a specific ionic microstep.
edges.subject: e255q-versus-wt

evidence.explanation: Figure 4A's D371N panel and Results support loss of sodium enhancement while showing residual binding; transport and binding are kept distinct.

edges.mechanism: D371N lacks WT-like sodium stimulation of the high-affinity component but retains increasing anisotropy as protein is added. This net response does not prove direct contact between D371 and sodium or absence of all transport activity.
edges.subject: d371n-versus-wt

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Historical AAF94694.1 D36/E255/D371 correspond to current Q9KRU4 D32/E251/D367, verified by sequence comparison. D32 lies in PF01554 17-176 and E251/D367 in 243-404. Current protein begins MHRY whereas the historical reference begins MENSVHRY; current sequence is M plus historical residues 6-461, not simply historical residues 5-461. Mutant labels refer to the paper's numbering, not current UniProt coordinates.
causal_graphs.limitations: Directness describes the purified-protein binding response, not an observed atomic sodium-coordination or transport step. WT sodium enhancement is strongest at low protein concentrations; the curves converge at high concentration. Single mutants retain binding. Apparent two-component fits do not independently count sites. Supplementary expression/purity controls were not inspected, so equivalent folding is not established. Li+, Cs+ and Rb+ do not mimic the WT sodium response in this assay.

causal_graphs.scope: Purified N-terminal His10-tagged NorM-VC WT and single substitutions D36N, E255Q and D371N, Raturi 2021 Figure 4A; paper residue numbering retained.
causal_graphs.title: Sodium enhances low-concentration ethidium binding in WT but not three NorM-VC variants

causal_graphs.context: No added sodium; 0.2 uM purified WT protein and 2 uM ethidium in the DDM/KPi binding assay. Buffer pH is varied from 6 to 9 in 0.2 steps with concentrated KOH. Anisotropy uses 500/580 nm and about 2 min equilibration; three independent protein batches, mean +/- SEM. This is not the glucose-energized cell assay.

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 4B, biochemical Results and binding Methods establish the direction under fixed-protein conditions, separately from the sodium titration.

edges.mechanism: WT anisotropy increases with two transitions across the tested pH range. The net biochemical response is retained without promoting the authors' residue-specific pKa assignments to observed molecular events.
edges.subject: raise-buffer-ph

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Intact historical 461-aa NorM-VC maps to Q9KRU4 sequence version 2 with the verified initiation difference and four-position internal numbering offset. Both current PF01554 intervals, 17-176 and 243-404, belong to the tested protein context; neither repeat was isolated.
causal_graphs.limitations: The double-sigmoid response is observed, but assigning fitted midpoints 6.9 and 8.0 to specific carboxylates is an inference. Buffer alkalinization by KOH is the experimental intervention, not an independently controlled change of only one residue's protonation. This binding response is not an observed transport cycle or universal pH rule for the family.
